title: Improve coarse-resolution topology for thin sub-cell features
description:
## Summary
At coarse voxel resolutions (preview VPU ~5-10), thin authored parts whose cross-section is at or below the voxel cell size (e.g. a Finger capsule radius ~0.075 at cell 0.1-0.2) under-sample and produce missing triangles / broken / torn topology. This is independent of triangle winding (the W-02/W-03 fix on TSK-0119 is orthogonal) and independent of the skeleton terminal-node work owned by TSK-0048 (which explicitly does not claim an extraction/topology root cause). Reproduced by the user in the editor at Preview Mesh Quality 5-10 on thin fingers and other parts; disappears when the feature is thickened/lengthened or resolution is raised.

## User Mandate
> "But we still need to be more supportive of lower resolutions until we make generation faster. If your change is more towards correctness, then I think that's okay. But this is still an active area for making fixes"

STRICT. Any coarse-resolution robustness change must (1) not materially regress preview generation speed (field sampling / active-cell construction / contour resolution / mesh extraction / total) versus the recorded production baseline — TSK-0008 owns the benchmark gate; (2) not reintroduce per-triangle SDF evaluations, global orientation traversals, or large hot-path per-triangle allocations; (3) preserve the authoritative CreatureDefinition boundary, deterministic output, watertightness, and symmetry behavior. The resolution-vs-speed tradeoff for the specific approach still needs explicit user direction before a large change is accepted.

## Scope
- Reproduce the coarse-VPU missing-triangle failure with a minimal fixture: a body/hand + a thin sub-cell feature (e.g. capsule radius ~0.075) at VPU 5 and 10 (and one higher VPU as a control). Measure boundary/non-manifold edges and locate the torn region.
- Determine the root cause class: uniform-grid under-sampling of sub-cell geometry (likely) vs. a targeted extraction bug. Confirm it is independent of winding by re-running the topology audit with the winding fix applied.
- Evaluate cheap levers that reuse existing data (no new SDF eval): e.g. thin-feature-aware sampling guarantee, region-aware adaptive cell refinement near small parts, or a documented minimum resolution per feature. Benchmark each against the TSK-0008 baseline before accepting.
- Add a regression fixture + test asserting watertightness (0 boundary, 0 non-manifold) for a thin sub-cell feature at coarse VPU, and a directed-edge consistency check.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A minimal coarse-VPU thin-feature fixture reproduces the failure and is captured as a test.
- Root cause is documented (uniform-grid under-sampling vs. extraction bug), with winding ruled in/out.
- Any fix is benchmarked before/after and does not materially regress preview generation.
- The thin-feature coarse-VPU fixture becomes watertight (0 boundary, 0 non-manifold) and deterministically stable.
- Existing suites (Runtime PlayMode + Editor EditMode) remain green.

## Validation
- Unity: run the minimal fixture at VPU 5/10 + control; record triangle/boundary/non-manifold counts.
- Full Runtime PlayMode and Editor EditMode suites.
- dotnet build clean; git diff --check clean.
- Benchmark before/after against the TSK-0008 baseline (VPU10 ~204ms, VPU16 ~626ms total; extraction-only VPU16 133.5ms as reference).

## Findings
None yet — open item captured from user testing (2026-09-06).

## Blockers
Resolution-vs-speed approach choice still needs user direction for any large (e.g. adaptive refinement) change. Cheap, well-scoped fixes can proceed under the TSK-0008 perf gate.

## Next Step
Reproduce the coarse-VPU thin-feature failure with a minimal fixture and record the topology numbers; confirm independence from winding; then evaluate the cheapest lever against the benchmark baseline before any implementation.

comments.body:
ROUND 2 (BeastMaster) — bounded repro + root-cause + characterization fixture. No production code changed; test-only. No commit/push (orchestrator commits).

## Measured topology (PlayMode, on main e88ba5d, winding fix e1b078a applied)
Minimal body/hand + thin-finger fixture (palm sphere r0.4 @ origin + long thin finger capsule r0.075 h2.2 axis Y @ y0.45, blend 0.05; bounds 1/2.2/1):
- VPU 5 (cell 0.2): tri=120 verts=90 boundary=8 nonManifold=0 totalEdge=184 -> NOT watertight (TORN).
- VPU 10 (cell 0.1): tri=672 boundary=0 -> watertight.
- VPU 16 control: tri=2072 boundary=0 -> watertight.
Free thin finger (r0.075, sub-cell) same bounds at VPU 10: tri=0 (feature DROPPED by under-sampling); VPU 32 control: tri=1504 watertight.
Characterization fixture is deterministic (repeat extraction equal).

## Root-cause class + winding
Uniform-grid under-sampling of sub-cell geometry (not a targeted extraction bug, not winding). Evidence: every torn result shows ONLY boundary edges (open holes) with 0 non-manifold edges; a winding inversion cannot open a boundary hole, and results reproduce on current main with W-02/W-03 (e1b078a) applied, so winding is orthogonal and ruled out. Coarse VPU either drops the thin feature (0 tris) or leaves an open boundary; raising resolution resolves it to watertight — resolution (sampling) dependent, not a geometry defect.

## Changed files (test-only)
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/CoarseThinFeatureTopologyTests.cs (new; characterization gate, green today, documents current torn/dropped coarse-VPU behavior and points at TSK-0129; a robust-coarse fix must update it to watertight/present).
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/CoarseThinFeatureTopologyTests.cs.meta (Unity-generated).

## Validation
- dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore: Build succeeded, 0 warnings/0 errors, exit 0.
- Unity PlayMode focused CoarseThinFeatureTopologyTests: 2/2 passed.
- Unity PlayMode full ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime: 526/526 passed, 0 failed.
- git diff --check: clean (exit 0).

## No benchmark
No production lever added in this round (test-only fixture), so no before/after benchmark vs the TSK-0008 baseline is required per round scope.

## Next step
Fix requires user direction on the resolution-vs-speed tradeoff (mandate + blocker). Cheapest data-reuse levers to evaluate before any implementation: region-aware adaptive cell refinement near small parts, or documented minimum resolution per feature — each must be benchmarked vs TSK-0008 baseline (VPU10 ~204ms / VPU16 ~626ms total; extraction-only VPU16 133.5ms) before acceptance.

comments.body:
ROUND 1 (BeastMaster, sprint) — lever evaluation. Reproduced on fixed point 74e2ed9 and evaluated the bounded data-reuse levers; STOPPED before implementing because no bounded lever satisfies all STRICT mandate constraints simultaneously. No production code changed; no commit/push.

## Reproduction confirmed (this build, HEAD 74e2ed9)
- Full Runtime PlayMode (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime): 526/526 passed, 0 failed (run via MCP, assembly-scoped).
- Focused CoarseThinFeatureTopologyTests: 2/2 passed (gate green — asserts current torn/dropped coarse behavior).
- dotnet build Runtime 0/0; Tests.Runtime 0/0. git diff --check exit 0. No files touched (worktree shows only concurrent animation-workstream files, untouched).
- Morphology extraction unchanged since the ROUND 2 repro (e88ba5d→74e2ed9 only added TSK-0082 validation split), so round-2 topology numbers (body VPU5 tri=120 boundary=8 torn; free r0.075 VPU10 tri=0 dropped; higher VPU watertight) still hold.

## Lever evaluation (data-reuse, no new SDF eval) — root cause is uniform-grid under-sampling of sub-cell geometry
The three mandate-listed cheap levers are all RESOLUTION levers; none is resolution-free, and each collides with a hard constraint:
1) Thin-feature-aware minimum-resolution/sampling guarantee (whole-grid VPU floor from existing per-op world AABBs). To make the body fixture (r0.075 finger) watertight at VPU5 (cell 0.2), cell must drop to ~r (0.075) → internal VPU ~13-14 → ~2.8x per axis → ~20x+ sample/cell volume on the WHOLE creature. That IS the user's real thin-finger preview scenario, so it materially regresses preview speed → violates mandate #1 (no material regression vs TSK-0008 baseline) and undercuts "be more supportive of LOWER resolutions." Only defensible if the tradeoff is user-directed and it is provably inactive on the benchmark creature (which I cannot verify: no committed benchmark harness exists; the ~204/626ms fixture/methodology is not reproducible in-repo this round).
2) Region-aware adaptive cell refinement near small parts. This is the technically correct fix (raise sampling only in thin-part regions) but is a local-adaptive-refinement change — explicitly a STOP boundary this round and, per mandate, needs user direction before a large change. Also high risk for watertight seams/welding/determinism at region boundaries.
3) Documented minimum resolution per feature. Same global-floor cost/benefit as (1); a documentation-only change does not make the fixture watertight.
- Rejected: per-triangle SDF or a global orientation traversal (mandate #2) and any second extraction path (STOP). A winding change cannot close boundary holes (root cause ruled winding out in ROUND 2).

## Decision / blocker
The genuinely-sub-cell fixtures cannot be made watertight/present at coarse VPU by any lever that keeps uniform coarse sampling AND avoids the (forbidden) local-refinement path. The only levers that meet the acceptance are resolution levers whose resolution-vs-speed tradeoff the mandate says needs explicit user direction, and which cannot be benchmark-gated this round because the TSK-0008 gate fixture is not reproducible in-repo (no committed harness). Per the round's stop-guidance and the mandate, I did NOT guess a lever.

## Next step (needs orchestrator/user)
Pick the lever to proceed under user direction on the resolution-vs-speed tradeoff: (A) local refinement near thin parts only (correct, more scope, needs a before/after benchmark), or (B) global minimum-resolution floor (small code, but ~20x cost on thin-featured creatures and must be shown inactive on the benchmark creature). Before either, land a committed, reproducible GenerateData benchmark (VPU10/VPU16 total + FieldSampling/ActiveCell/Contour/Extraction sub-stages) so the TSK-0008 gate is actually verifiable in-repo. Status left Ready.
